headline: Open Interpreter’s default filesystem and shell access can amplify marker outputs into prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marker is a document-processing agent with no filesystem write or network egress, while Open Interpreter reads/writes the filesystem and can execute shell commands. If marker’s document output is copied into Open Interpreter or placed in a shared workspace, Open Interpreter may treat attacker-controlled document text as instructions. The shared filesystem bridge makes this plausible in default pair usage.
conditions: IF marker output is copied into a file that Open Interpreter reads
IF both agents share a writable workspace on the same machine
mitigations: Keep marker outputs in a read-only export folder
Disable Open Interpreter access to the marker output directory
Require manual review before Open Interpreter processes any marker-generated file
Use separate OS users for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files and reject untrusted document text

B_data_leakage.rationale: marker itself has no filesystem or network access, but Open Interpreter can read the entire local filesystem and has broad network egress. If marker processes sensitive local documents and its outputs are then handled by Open Interpreter, sensitive content can be exposed to model providers or external APIs configured by the user. The pair therefore creates a default leakage path through shared local files.
conditions: IF marker is used on sensitive local documents
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to read the same workspace or filesystem subtree
mitigations: Store sensitive inputs outside Open Interpreter’s readable paths
Turn off Open Interpreter network access for sensitive runs
Use a separate machine or VM for Open Interpreter
Delete intermediate marker outputs after use
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marker does not write files, but Open Interpreter has unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and modify_git_state. In a shared workspace, Open Interpreter can overwrite or commit artifacts that marker produced, and the concurrency model explicitly says shared state is via filesystem. Because the pair lacks locking and Open Interpreter’s defaults are powerful, write conflicts can corrupt outputs or git state.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory tree
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to modify git state or write artifacts that marker also uses
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared files
Disable git writes in Open Interpreter for shared projects
Use filesystem locks around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: marker produces document-processing outputs, and Open Interpreter can act on local files and shell commands. If Open Interpreter treats marker’s extracted text or structure as authoritative without verification, downstream actions can be taken on incorrect or adversarial document content. The pair’s default workflow makes this a realistic cascade, though not inherently irreversible in every case.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes marker output as input without human verification
IF the output is used to drive shell commands or file edits
mitigations: Require a human check before any action based on marker output
Use a validation step that compares extracted text to source documents
Disable auto-run in Open Interpreter
Limit Open Interpreter to read-only review mode
requires-engineering: add schema validation for marker outputs

E_compliance.rationale: marker is open-source document processing with no stated residency controls, while Open Interpreter can access local files and send prompts to configured model providers. If marker handles regulated documents and Open Interpreter forwards derived content to third-party providers, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The risk is compliance mismatch rather than a guaranteed violation, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by marker
IF Open Interpreter sends derived content to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workflow
Use a provider with suitable contractual terms
Disable network egress for compliance-sensitive runs
Keep audit logs of what content leaves the machine
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
